source.text: A private network contains application and data subnets. Only application-to-data access is permitted; every other origin-to-data access is denied. The policy aims to restrict data access to the application. To check a request, identify its origin and compare it with the permitted application origin: application is allowed, all other origins are denied. No cost, ROI, availability, performance or compliance measurements are provided.

objective.0: No observable source-based aim, or the activity contradicts the declared aim and audience needs.
objective.1: An observable aim is present but the item practices only part of it or needs clarification.
objective.2: An observable aim states an action and source concept; the item and expected evidence directly practice it at an accessible audience level.

cognitive_process.0: The item performs a different process from the declared activity; naming Bloom alone earns no credit.
cognitive_process.1: The intended process is partly practiced but its reasoning or verification is incomplete.
cognitive_process.2: The activity actually practices the declared process and makes the answer, reasoning or verification observable, when supported by the source.

fidelity.0: A factual or numerical claim contradicts the source or invents unsupported information.
fidelity.1: No contradiction is apparent, but the supporting source connection or an important limitation is unclear.
fidelity.2: Claims and expected answers are traceable to the supplied source; analogies are bounded and unavailable evidence is not invented.

format.0: Invalid JSON or missing required content/item fields.
format.1: JSON and fields are present but a format instruction is violated, such as an ambiguous quiz answer.
format.2: Valid existing content/item shape and all applicable format instructions, including four quiz options and a determinate answer.

rubric.decision: Pass requires at least 7/8, every dimension at least 1, fidelity exactly 2 and format exactly 2. Review content before assigning scores; valid JSON and prompt coverage alone never establish quality.

samples.objective: Identify the two subnets and explain their access relationship using a bounded analogy.

content.titulo: Two areas of a private network
content.introduccion_contextualizada: Identify application and data subnets and explain their access relationship. Think of two named rooms; this analogy explains separation, not additional network behavior.

items.frente: Which two subnets does the source name, and which one may access data?
items.dorso: The application and data subnets. Only the application may access data; every other origin is denied.
items.pista_didactica: Two named rooms: the application room has permission to enter the data room. The analogy does not add security guarantees.

rationale.objective: Naming the two subnets and explaining who may access data fulfills the introduction's aim in accessible language.
rationale.cognitive_process: The front prompts recall; the back explains the access relationship and the hint bounds the analogy.
rationale.fidelity: Subnet names and allowed/denied origins are explicit in the source; no security guarantees are added.
rationale.format: The content has the existing three fields and a nonempty front, back and hint.

samples.evidence_excerpt: Only the application may access data

samples.objective: Apply the documented origin rule and verify the expected decision for two requests.

content.introduccion_contextualizada: Apply the documented rule to application and other origins, then verify each decision. This is a policy exercise, not a deployment command.

items.titulo_paso: Compare each origin with the permitted application origin
items.descripcion: For application-to-data, select allowed. For another origin-to-data, select denied. Follow the source's origin-comparison procedure.
items.verificacion: Check the decisions against the source: application allowed, any other origin denied. No live network result is claimed.

rationale.objective: The step executes the stated two-request exercise with explicit observable decisions.
rationale.cognitive_process: Comparing origins applies the supplied procedure; verification names both expected results.
rationale.fidelity: Both decisions follow the source, and no missing CLI command or live outcome is invented.
rationale.format: The numbered step, action title, description and verification are present; optional code is null.

samples.evidence_excerpt: application allowed, any other origin denied

samples.objective: Apply the same Junior/Senior origin rule and distinguish supported from unsupported conclusions.

content.introduccion_contextualizada: Apply the origin rule and analyze the alternatives. Junior and Senior share these pedagogical expectations; this quiz does not define a higher Senior tier.

items.pregunta: Another origin requests data access. Which conclusion follows from the source?
items.justificacion_didactica: A follows the denial of every other origin. B contradicts that rule. C and D cannot be inferred because the source gives no ROI or availability measurements.
items.pista_didactica: Compare the request origin with the sole permitted application origin.

rationale.objective: The question applies the shared rule to a case and asks the learner to distinguish conclusions.
rationale.cognitive_process: The explanation contrasts a supported answer, a contradiction and unsupported metrics.
rationale.fidelity: The answer follows the denial rule; numerical/availability distractors are explicitly rejected, not asserted.
rationale.format: Four alternatives, an exact correct option, explanation of each alternative and a hint are present.

samples.evidence_excerpt: A follows the denial of every other origin

samples.objective: Explain the permitted and denied cases visually, without requiring unsupported architectural trade-offs.

content.introduccion_contextualizada: Explain both access cases using the documented boundary. The source supplies no competing architecture or availability evidence, so this scene does not require Evaluate.

items.narrativa: Application-to-data is allowed; every other origin-to-data is denied. Explain how this implements the stated aim of restricting data access to the application.
items.recurso_visual: Two labeled subnets with an allowed application-to-data arrow and a crossed-out other-origin-to-data arrow.

rationale.objective: The scene explains the stated boundary and makes its two cases visible.
rationale.cognitive_process: Narration and diagram explain the source relationship; cognition follows the activity rather than a rigid leader tier.
rationale.fidelity: Only documented access cases and the source aim are presented; unavailable trade-offs are acknowledged.
rationale.format: The scene contains a block, narration and a concrete matching visual resource.

samples.evidence_excerpt: Application-to-data is allowed; every other origin-to-data is denied

samples.objective: Explain the policy's documented impact and justify a recommendation against its stated access criterion.

content.titulo: Keep access aligned with the documented aim
content.introduccion_contextualizada: Explain the documented access restriction and justify retaining the rule using the source criterion, not invented ROI or compliance results.

items.impacto: Other origins are denied, matching the stated aim of restricting data access to the application.
items.recomendacion: Retain that rule to satisfy the stated application-only criterion. No costs, ROI or compliance measurements are supplied; obtain separate evidence before drawing those conclusions.

rationale.objective: The item explains the actual restriction and justifies a decision using the documented aim.
rationale.cognitive_process: The recommendation evaluates the rule against the explicit application-only criterion, rather than merely naming Evaluate.
rationale.fidelity: Access impact is supported; unavailable business metrics and compliance evidence are explicitly bounded.
rationale.format: Concept, impact and justified recommendation use existing executive-summary fields.

samples.evidence_excerpt: Retain that rule to satisfy the stated application-only criterion

samples.objective: Identify the two subnet names and explain their roles in accessible language.

content.introduccion_contextualizada: Identify the two subnets and explain their roles.

items.frente: Justify the ingress-policy invariant by evaluating permitted and denied origin classes.
items.dorso: Only application-to-data is permitted; the policy meets the application-only criterion by denying every other origin.

rationale.objective: The item never asks for both subnet names or accessible roles; unexplained specialist phrasing contradicts the declared beginner aim.
rationale.cognitive_process: The question demands evaluation/justification instead of the declared recall/explanation activity; its hint repeats jargon without scaffolding.
rationale.fidelity: The policy claim and application-only criterion remain source-supported: this is not a hallucination example.
rationale.format: Valid JSON and nonempty front, back and hint satisfy the existing flashcard structure despite pedagogical misalignment.
